description:
Order the cartographer agent to design a map: of a NEW location (a new textId)
        |or a REGENERATION of an existing one (a textId from availableMaps — for example, to fix "the topology is wrong").
        |You do NOT draw the grid and legend — you write a BRIEF, the cartographer will design it at the nearest transition,
        |and you will see the finished map in the "DESIGNED MAP" snapshot
        |(take the coordinates for MAP_BATTLE tasks from there).
        |
        |⚠️ A map is a reusable asset of the LOCATION, not decoration of a visit: in structure describe
        |entrances/exits as properties of the PLACE (there may be none or many), NOT "where the
        |party enters from" — you will decide this visit's entry point by placing tokens (a MAP_BATTLE task).
        |The brief's contract is the same as for tasks to implementors: facts and intent exhaustively (the cartographer does not
        |see the book or your thoughts), execution is up to them.
name: designMap

textId.description: Map textId — slug [a-z0-9-]+. New (creation) or existing from availableMaps (regeneration).

description.description: Artistic description of the location (visible to the player).

idea.description: The IDEA — a spatial challenge in one phrase: what the player will DO in this space ("blind combat in a closing fog", "sneak between patrols", "hold the door against a crowd"). Come up with it from the surroundings, the story and common sense — the cartographer will build the grid AROUND it.

function.description: Function of the place: what it is and why it is in the plot ("a fortified cellar refuge of a paranoid gardener, a defense hub").

narrativeContext.description: Narrative context: who lives/lived here, what happened — defines the setting of the rooms.

tactics.description: Tactical requirements: whether a battle is expected, how many participants, what must be possible (cover, distances, maneuvering routes). Optional.

structure.description: LOCATION structure: its entrances/exits (properties of the place, not of the visit!), key objects, zone links. Optional.

hazards.description: Hazards with mechanics: what, where, DC, damage, trigger. Optional.

visibility.description: Visibility: what the characters recognize at the threshold, what is HIDDEN (the hidden gets no label on the map). Optional.

baseBookLocationTextId.description: A book location as a basis: the textId of a book location with a ready grid — the cartographer will receive its grid as a starting point (edits it per the brief, does not draw from scratch). For tweaking a book location to the game; if the grid should not be touched but taken as is — use instantiateBookLocation instead of designMap. Usually null.

closesTaskId.description: Optional. ID of the task or issue that is FULLY resolved by THIS call — pass it OPTIMISTICALLY when you are confident in the arguments. If the call returns an error, the wrapper itself will NOT close the task. Don't use it for partial progress; for multi-tool tasks, close via completeTask after the final step.

description:
🗺️📕 Materialize a book location with a READY tactical grid into a game map — WITHOUT the cartographer.
        |When to call: the book has a developed location with a grid (it has a grid) — take it as is, do NOT order designMap from scratch. Instant and free: the book's grid/legend/dimensions are carried over 1:1, the map image renders itself.
        |If the book grid needs TWEAKING for a particular game — not this tool, but designMap with baseBookLocationTextId (the cartographer will refine it).
        |The location was already materialized in this game earlier (a map with this textId exists) — it will simply switch the active one to it, without re-rendering.
name: instantiateBookLocation

textId.description: textId of the book location (from the book structure, the locations[*].textId field).

closesTaskId.description: Optional. ID of the task or issue that is FULLY resolved by THIS call — pass it OPTIMISTICALLY when you are confident in the arguments. If the call returns an error, the wrapper itself will NOT close the task. Don't use it for partial progress; for multi-tool tasks, close via completeTask after the final step.

description:
📕🗺️ Put a location into the BOOK for FUTURE games of this book (reuse). This is NOT a local edit of the current game's map — this is the book's canon: the location will become available to the planner of any future playthrough. A repeat promote of the same textId OVERWRITES the book location (a deliberate decision).
        |When to call: you designed a location (description + grid) IN THIS turn with value beyond the current game — a place the story may return to, a node of the book's map. Promote IMMEDIATELY in the same turn you designed it: decisions do NOT make it into the book, the only channel into future games of this book is promote, a deferred promote = lost canon. You pass the descriptive part as an object; take the tactical grid MECHANICALLY from an already existing game map via gridFromMapTextId (do not rewrite the grid by hand).
name: promoteToBookLocation

location.description: Descriptive part of a book location (textId/name/description/ambient/POI/hazards/interactives). The grid field may be left empty if you take the grid from a map via gridFromMapTextId.

textId.description: Slug identifier of the location, format [a-z0-9-]+. Used via `AiBookNode.locationTextId`.

name.description: Title: "Crater of the Star Forge", "The Baron's Throne Room", "The Cult's Assembly Hall".

description.description: General description of the space: what kind of place it is, what is characteristic, what the players see right at the entrance. 2-4 sentences.

ambient.description: Atmosphere and physical parameters: light, sound, smell, scale. Helps the planner run the scene immersively.

light.description: Lighting: "dusk", "bright daylight with dusty streaks", "dark, only torches by the doors", "pulsing light of rune columns".

sound.description: Sound background: "silence and dripping water", "the roar of machines and shouting", "distant chanting of monks", "crackling fire in the hearth".

smell.description: Smell (optional): "the smell of burnt metal and sweat", "ozone and perfume", "rotting seaweed". Helps immersion a lot.

scale.description: Scale/dimensions: "a hall 100×80 ft, ceiling 100 ft", "a cave 30×30 ft", "an open crater, diameter 300 ft". Helps the planner estimate distances for movement/spells.

grid.description: Text matrix of the map (optional). Only for tactical locations (battles/puzzles) where the relative position of objects is critical. For social/exploration without combat — null.

widthCells.description: Map width in cells = number of characters in each row.

heightCells.description: Map height in cells = number of rows.

mapGrid.description: Text map. One symbol = one cell. Rows are separated by a real newline (`\n` in a JSON-encoded string = a real newline character). The service automatically normalizes accidental double-escapes (a literal `\n`) and adjusts widthCells/heightCells to the actual grid. The map holds only static terrain and objects; mark the encounter participants' starting positions with a separate symbol + a legend entry with relatedTextId pointing to the participant.

legend.description: Legend: every symbol used in `mapGrid` is described by a separate entry. An entry has: name (a short name — for the UI/planner), description (a full description with mechanics), relatedTextId (optional — to an interactive/hazard/POI/participant).

symbol.description: Symbol — EXACTLY ONE character (a letter a-z/A-Z, a digit 0-9 or one of +-*=/|:;,~^@#%&). Case matters: 'H' and 'h' are different symbols. By itself it means nothing — the meaning is in `name`+`description`. Within one map a symbol must be unique; on different maps the same symbol may mean different things.

name.description: A short artistic caption for the PLAYER over the map (optional, STINGY — 0-4 per map): "Isolde's Altar", "Well", "Forge". ONLY for key visible buildings/objects. WITHOUT name: base terrain (floor/walls/water), decorative props, the HIDDEN (traps/caches — the caption would spoil them) and "starting positions" (the party's entry point is a property of the visit, settled by tokens, not by the map).

description.description: Full description with mechanical details: "a stone wall 5×5×10ft, AC 18, 20 HP, immune to poison and psychic, collapses when HP is lost", "an oil barrel — partial cover (+2 AC); when hit by fire it ignites in a 10ft radius for 3d6 fire". Must be enough for the turn planner to run the scene without consulting a PDF.

relatedTextId.description: textId of the related entity — if the symbol denotes an interactive (`location.interactives[].textId`), a hazard (`location.hazards[].textId`), a POI (`location.pointsOfInterest[].textId`) or an encounter participant. Null if the symbol denotes plain terrain (floor/wall/cover with no special rules).

cellSizeFeet.description: Size of one cell in feet. 5 by default (D&D standard). For large-scale maps (crater, battlefield) — 10/20 ft.

orientation.description: Orientation: "N=up", "entrance from the south". Optional, but desirable for battles where direction matters.

pointsOfInterest.description: Points of interest (POI): numbered/named areas of the location with their own description. At least 1 for a tactical location; for a simple one — may be 0 (then `description` suffices).

textId.description: Slug identifier of the POI, format [a-z0-9-]+. Unique within the location.

label.description: Display label: "1", "A", "BOSS", "N". The same as in `grid.cells` if the POI is on the map.

name.description: POI name: "Broken Bridge", "Acid Lake", "Altar of Isolde".

description.description: Description: what the players see/find/can do. 2-5 sentences. Includes game-mechanical details (check DCs, effects) where appropriate.

gridPosition.description: Position on the map: "row 5, col 12" or "x:12, y:5". Null if the POI is not on the grid (for example, for a location without a grid).

hazards.description: Hazards built into the location: traps, the environment (acid/lava/collapse), magical effects. Each has a telegraph/trigger/effect/at least 3 ways to get around it.

name.description: Title: "Acid Fumes", "Lava Field", "Floor Snare Trap", "Magical Sleep".

telegraph.description: Telegraph: a noticeable sign of danger **before the player steps in**. "The water is bright turquoise, acrid fumes", "cracks in the floor, a dark crust", "the hum is growing". Without it the danger turns into a "gotcha" — a punishment for the player's inattention.

trigger.description: Trigger condition: "a creature within 10ft of the water", "weight >100 pounds on the plate", "opening the door without dispelling the charm", "6+ rounds in the zone".

effect.description: Effect under targetLevel: "DC 15 Con save, 21 (6d6) acid damage on a failure, half on a success", "fall 30ft taking 10 (3d6) bludgeoning damage", "polymorph into a sheep for 1 hour".

waysToAvoid.description: At least 3 independent ways to detect/bypass/disarm. "Perception DC 12 to notice the cracks", "Detect Magic reveals the outline", "Jump over the zone (Athletics DC 14)", "Use the ring of resistance".

justification.description: Justification in the fiction: why the hazard is here — a link to the inhabitants' scheme, the nature of the place, history. "Acid seeps from a cracked rune stone under the star", "Brimskarda set it up to hold the dragon". Helps the planner fit it into the narrative.

escalation.description: Spread rule for escalating hazards (advancing water/fire/gas/collapse): "expands by 5ft each round", "doubles damage after round 3", "after 2 rounds the zone covers the whole map". Null — a static hazard. Creates time pressure in space: drives fighters into the desired zones.

escalationTrigger.description: Escalation start condition: "when the alarm is raised", "after round 3", "when the boss is below 50% HP", "when a column is broken". Null — the escalation is active from the start of the scene. Fill in if `escalation != null`.

interactives.description: Interactive objects for combat arenas: a chandelier-that-can-be-cut-down, oil-barrels-by-a-torch, a lever-that-drops-the-portcullis, a collapsible-wall. One unexpected interactive object changes the whole battle — it is not decoration but an accomplice. For non-combat locations usually empty.

name.description: Title: "Oil Candelabra", "Bridge Support Chain", "Water Sluice Lever", "Alchemical Barrels", "Swinging Rope".

gridPosition.description: Position on the map: "row 5, col 12" or "x:12, y:5". If the object is spread out (wall/chain) — a zone description.

description.description: Description: what it is, what it looks like, what makes it noticeable. 1-2 sentences.

trigger.description: Activation trigger: what the player (or enemy) must do. "Cut the rope (Athletics DC 12)", "Atk +5 vs AC 13", "Set it on fire with a fire spell", "Push (Athletics DC 15)", "Use key X". Must be achievable in combat.

effect.description: Activation effect: what happens after the trigger. Concretely — DC/damage/area/timing. "The chandelier falls onto cells B3-D5, 22 (4d10) bludgeoning, DC 15 Dex saving throw for half", "The portcullis drops, blocking the south exit for 1 minute", "The barrels explode: 3d6 fire in a 10ft radius".

usableBy.description: Who can use it: PARTY (the party only), ENEMIES (the enemies only), BOTH (both sides — the enemies too can cut the chain to drop it on the party). Who can use an interactive object in the arena: Par=the party only (the heroes' lever), Ene=the enemies only (an enemy ritual/device), Bot=both sides (a shared lever/altar).

oneShot.description: Whether it is single-use (`true` — after activation the object is spent, for example a fallen chandelier) or can trigger repeatedly (`false` — a lever can be used several times).

gridFromMapTextId.description: textId of a game map (from availableMaps or the current chosenMap) whose grid to MECHANICALLY convert into the book location's grid. null — leave location.grid as is (may be empty: a location without combat is legitimate).

If the call returns an error, the wrapper itself will NOT close the task. Don't use it for partial progress; for multi-tool tasks, close via completeTask after the final step.

description:
Record ONE NEW master's decision. Use when there is really one decision; for a batch of several decisions — `addDecisions([...])` in one tool call.

        |The decision is passed to all implementor agents and the verifier, saved in the turn's history and visible to the planners of the following turns. Use for:
        |1) DECISIONS ON PLAYER REQUESTS: if in playerMoves the player asks for something non-standard or points at an error of the previous generation — be sure to record your decision here, do not leave the interpretation to the implementors.
        |2) ATMOSPHERIC/CONCEPTUAL INSTRUCTIONS: the scene's general concept, tone, key context.
        |3) CANONICAL CALCULATIONS AND TURN RULES: total debuff values, cumulative counters, the interpretation of resistances — so that the implementors and the verifier do not recompute in their own way.
        |If a decision with that textId already exists — in this turn OR in the game's history — use updateDecision (this tool will return an error): a re-`add` would erase the grounds on which the node stands.
        |The master's decisions take priority over any playerMove and any D&D rules. The implementors and the verifier must follow them.
name: addDecision

decision.description:
Brief and unambiguous decision (NOT tone/atmosphere — that belongs in the NARRATIVE task's brief). Examples:
        |• 'APPROVED — add Shillelagh to Lily's prepared spells right in this turn as a FIX of an old generator error.'
        |• 'DENIED — Anomaly does not move this turn (she is right next to Lily, no point)'
        |• 'Total strength drain of Lilia = -10 (accumulated over past turns)'

reason.description: The decision's IDEA — WHY it exists, what scene/mechanics problem it solves — the essence in ONE phrase. Not a retelling of the decision in other words: turn diagnostics is read from the ideas.

basedOn.description: References to grounds: `decision:<textId>` — another decision (of this turn, the story or the chapter, any status); `move:<ref>` — a request/choice of the player of the CURRENT turn, addressed by the character's name or its textId; `action:<textId>` — a roll (action) of this turn or the story; `book:<textId>` — a book node; `part:<round>:<partId>` — a specific narration part (what the master said to the player: a promise, an NPC line, a scene detail), the part's address is visible in the parts snapshot. Parenthood is causal ("why it happened") or contextual ("where it was introduced").

description: ⏳ Advance in-game time by N minutes — for narrative gaps: rest, travel, waiting, "by evening". The time of the one whose request you are now playing out moves (there is no common world clock: each participant has their own time, only a sync point reconciles them). Time moves only through explicit tools: a player's turn by itself (and even more so a META turn) does NOT tick time, time does not go backward. `reason` is SAVED along with the turn: it is later used to reconstruct why the time jumped.

description:
Update a previously recorded master's decision (by exact textId). Use to bring canonical numbers and wordings up to date (the total strength drain changed, a new interpretation of a disputed question appeared) and to RE-HANG the grounds (a new basedOn). Do not breed duplicates via addDecision — for an existing textId always use updateDecision.

        |Works on a HISTORY decision too (past turns, the chapter's canon): history is immutable, so editing a historical node becomes its NEW VERSION in this turn — unset fields are inherited from the previous version, the status is kept. This way a retcon does not erase graph edges. In an ADD-ON (a lite pass) editing the canon of past turns is unavailable — only your own nodes; a contradiction with the canon is not recorded on top — play out the request without this edit, leave the contradiction to the scene master for the future.
name: updateDecision

textId.description: textId of an existing decision — of this turn or of the story. If there is no decision anywhere — an error; use addDecision.

decision.description: New decision text (fully replaces the old one). Not set — the previous text is kept (you edit only the grounds/idea).

reason.description: New decision IDEA — WHY it exists, in one phrase (fully replaces the old one). Not set — the previous idea is kept.

basedOn.description: References to grounds: `decision:<textId>` — another decision (of this turn, the story or the chapter, any status); `move:<ref>` — a request/choice of the player of the CURRENT turn, addressed by the character's name or its textId; `action:<textId>` — a roll (action) of this turn or the story; `book:<textId>` — a book node; `part:<round>:<partId>` — a specific narration part (what the master said to the player: a promise, an NPC line, a scene detail), the part's address is visible in the parts snapshot. Parenthood is causal ("why it happened") or contextual ("where it was introduced"). Not set — the previous grounds are kept; an empty array — removes them.

description:
📕 Declare a character GENERATED or REFINED in THIS game as the CANONICAL prototype of a book NPC — all future games of THIS book will materialize this NPC from it (a ready sheet + adaptation to the scene), rather than molding from scratch. The main case: a boss/named NPC of the book, played out well once, becomes the default for ALL playthroughs.
        |When to call: after you created (or an existing scene NPC acquired) a worthy, canonically complete significant NPC — ESPECIALLY bosses and named faces. The significance of such: bosses — at least MAJOR, named/book faces — LEAD.
        |Promotion is available for ANY significant NPC, not only structural ones. The key is strict: an NPC corresponding to a figure of the book's STRUCTURE (antagonist/keyNpcs — you see their textIds in the structure) is promoted STRICTLY under its structural textId — do not invent aliases (`grim-fang`, NOT `grim-fang-boss`); your own new slug is allowed ONLY for an NPC outside the structure. Do not promote random extras.
        |OVERWRITE: if you REFINED a character materialized from a previous book prototype (a clone) and the result is BETTER than the original — promote that too: a repeat promote will OVERWRITE the previous canon, and the book will get a new, improved default prototype. The criterion for re-promotion: overwrite the canon ONLY if the refinement improves the character's GENERAL TEXTURE (a fuller/better sheet, obvious defects of the canon fixed) — what will be useful to ANY future game; situational customization for the current game/scene (this game's states, memories, adaptations to the plot/party level) is NOT a reason: the canon is no place for the situational.
name: promoteToBookPrototype

description: ORDER THE SCENE'S POPULATION from the character specialist — in ONE call for everyone not yet in the game. You say WHO the scene needs and WHY; the sheet, stats, look, props and canonical address are assembled by the specialist (who will also look for a ready prototype in the library and in the book's canon) — you do not create characters yourself. ⏳ There will be NO result in THIS response: the order is executed at the end of the response, the finished faces will appear in the snapshot (the "📦 CHARACTER ORDERS" block) in the NEXT response — and there you will place tokens for them (`updateToken`) and promote the significant ones into the book's canon. Do not go into review in the same response: the transition into SELF_REVIEW will be rejected until the order has returned. A repeat call — a SECOND batch of faces, not a reminder of the first. The specialist is entitled to DECLINE an individual order (the reason will come in the same snapshot) — then you decide: stage the scene without this face or go up a level. NOT via an order: introduce an existing off-frame character via `enterScene` with the UUID and visibility from the canonical context; if they are already in another scene — via `transferScene`; leaving off-frame — `leaveScene`. Change visibility via `showCharacter`/`hideCharacter`, final deletion — only `removeFromGame`.
name: orderCast

orders.description: A batch of orders — one element per ROLE, at most 6 roles per call. Do not multiply elements for same-type extras: that is ONE batch element.

role.description: Who this is to the scene — role/function in words: "innkeeper", "guard sergeant", "syndicate liaison".

request.description: The order in words: why the scene needs the face, what it is busy with, what stands out, what is known about it from the book and the master's decisions. Self-sufficient — your scene's specialist does not see it.

significance.description: SIGNIFICANCE — your decision, not the specialist's (the scale is in the "🎯 SIGNIFICANCE" block of your instruction): BACKGROUND — a nameless extra; MINOR — a passing face of this scene; MAJOR — a figure the story will return to; LEAD — a key face of the campaign. Be STINGY: both the depth of the sheet and the level of the portrayal depend on it.

presence.description: Whether the face is OFF-FRAME: OFFSTAGE — it is NOT in the scene, it keeps driving events from off-frame (the second entry of the materialization criterion) — the server will set standby status, no token is needed; ONSTAGE — stands in the scene, needs a token on the grid.

anyOf.description: Non-empty list of canonical observer UUIDs.

name.description: Name, if it ALREADY exists in the book or was heard in the game. null — the specialist will invent a name.

textIdHint.description: The BASE OF THE ADDRESS in Latin letters — a short role slug (`dock-foreman`, `tavern-keeper`). The server will pick a free address and return the actual one; Cyrillic cannot become an address, so without a hint the face gets a faceless `npc-2`.

count.description: How many IDENTICAL (by scale [scale]) units are needed. 1 — one unit; the series cap is 8, more is several orders for different roles.

scale.description: WHAT ONE unit of `count` represents: INDIVIDUAL — a separate creature with its own sheet (with count>1 the specialist will make series clones and differentiate them with distinctions — it does not stamp identical ones); SWARM — ONE sheet represents the WHOLE CROWD (an HP pool, the "Swarm" trait, crowd damage) — this is not a number but a stat block FORM: SWARM with count=2 means TWO crowds (for example, goblin squads from different flanks).

props.description: CANONICAL PROPS AS A LIST — items that must end up in their inventory ("a tube with papers", "a warehouse key", "a guild seal"): what is not in the sheet cannot be handed over, taken away or searched. Prose in the order text does not count — list them.

guidance.description: Recommendations: tone, origin, manner, place in the scene. Do not dictate mechanics (stats, hp, attacks) — that is the specialist's.

bookNpcTextId.description: Book CANON key: the textId of a figure from the adventure structure (`antagonist`/`keyNpcs`) OR a key from the "📕 CANONICAL BOOK NPC PROTOTYPES" block (the registry pinned by past games — it also has faces outside the structure), if you are ordering precisely that figure: the specialist will take the ready canonical prototype instead of molding anew. A face outside the book's canon — null.

description: CANCEL a sync point: the scheduled event has become IRRELEVANT and will no longer happen — "wolves attack at night in the forest", but the party spent the night in a tavern; "we leave through the yard", but a fight broke out in the yard. The world stops waiting for it, the address is freed (if they want it — you will set it again), the canceled point no longer travels in the context. ⛔ This is NOT `completeSyncPoint`: there the event HAPPENED and has an outcome, here it did NOT happen and there is no outcome. The participants' played-out contributions remain canon — Cleve stood up and walked to the door, and in the narrative he does not teleport back to the table; only the failed event itself is canceled. Cancel a point when its meaning is exhausted, NOT because of a scene relocation: the point's scope is shown in the list of open ones (`scope:`), a point with the scope "until the end of the game" survives a relocation. ⏳ The cancellation takes effect together with your work — and, like processing, survives escalation.
name: cancelSyncPoint

textId.description: Address of the point being released.

reason.description: WHY the event will no longer happen — to the point ("the party is spending the night in the tavern, nobody will go into the forest until morning", "the fight started earlier — the departure through the yard is canceled").

description: PROCESS a sync point: the event HAPPENED, the world no longer waits for it. One tool for all cases of a taken-place event, the difference is in the OUTCOME: "everyone arrived and it is played out" / "we waited for the event — it occurred" / "we did not wait, I release". The outcome is written RELATIVE to the point's `condition`: check against it and name HOW the condition resolved ("Borya cast Shield — the reaction is played out"), not "time to close". ⛔ If you release one who HAS NOT YET ARRIVED — DO NOT INVENT a decision, consent or line for them: the snapshot honestly marks which of the addressees has had NOT A SINGLE contribution yet (`joinSyncPoint` was not called for them) — there is nothing to lean on for such a one. Write the outcome FOR THE EVENT, not for the absent player ("the party crossed the bridge, Vasya lagged behind on the road"): the time reconciliation that the processing gives will itself bring them up to the point's moment, and they will pick up their line with the NEXT request — with the remainder they arrived with. The completeness of joins does not close the point by itself: the decision is always yours. ⛔ The event did NOT take place and will not take place — this is not processing, this is `cancelSyncPoint`: do not write "I cancel" here as an outcome, otherwise the world will remember the failed as happened. ⏳ Processing takes effect together with your work — and SURVIVES escalation (a terminal decision on a point is not thrown out together with the pass's draft, even if the pass itself is escalated as a full turn).
name: completeSyncPoint

textId.description: Address of the point being worked.

outcome.description: How the point's condition resolved: "everyone chose a path, the party crosses the bridge", "dawn has come", "Vasya did not answer — I let him go, the party leaves without him".

description: DECLARE A SYNC POINT — a new SCHEDULED EVENT: what will happen, WHEN (if the deadline is already known), with whom and under what condition. While the point is open, the scene does not move through it: participants play out their part up to its moment, and you play out the event itself when the moment has come. There can be several points at once — different events, different subgroups. ⛔ If the address is ALREADY TAKEN by an open point — a refusal, not an addition: this tool creates a NEW point and only it. If you want to fix an existing one — `setSyncPointDue`/`setSyncPointPlayers`/`setSyncPointTexts`, each changes exactly one thing. ⏱ `afterMinutes` — in how much game time the event OCCURS, counted FROM THE FURTHEST OF THIS POINT'S ADDRESSEES (there is no common world clock — each participant has their own time, and the point is set FORWARD so that it can be reached; the one who went furthest is already there, the others are on their way): 0 — right now (the fight begins), 480 — "in eight hours, at dawn". DO NOT SPECIFY if the deadline is NOT YET KNOWN — without a moment the point WAITS for a trigger ("scouts will return with news", "someone will find the entrance to the dungeon"), it is not a barrier: it holds nobody and does not ripen by itself, but stays in the context as an open wait. Once you learn the deadline — assign it with `setSyncPointDue`. The moment and `condition` are DIFFERENT things: the moment says WHEN the event approaches, the condition — under what circumstances it will happen at all ("wolves attack at night IN THE FOREST"). An event scheduled for midnight will not catch off guard those who do not sleep at midnight — that is the meaning of the moment. The moment works ON ITS OWN too: an event conditioned on nothing but the deadline has no condition at all. WHOSE axes these are and whether `condition` accepts a particular kind is stated in the kind's section in the point norms, not here. If it becomes clear the event will no longer happen (the party spent the night in a tavern) — cancel the point with `cancelSyncPoint`, do not close it with an outcome. ⏳ The declaration takes effect TOGETHER with your work — when the pass reaches the end and it goes to the player; escalation throws out the work, and with it the declared event.
name: declareSyncPoint

textId.description: Point address: slug [a-z0-9-]+ up to 64 characters, by the meaning of the event ('sp-path-choice', 'sp-ambush-reaction'). Already taken by an open point — the call will be REJECTED.

kind.description: Point kind — see the value descriptions. The point kind — which world event it stands for. Evt — a scheduled world event. Sre — the party's short rest (a halt). Lre — the party's long rest (a night's stay). Scc — a change of scenery: the party moves to another place. Ben — entering a battle; the same kind is used to bring reinforcements into a battle already under way. What stands behind each kind — what consequence processing it has, who processes it and what is NOT expected of you for this kind — is stated in the point rules, in the SECTION OF THIS KIND.

reason.description: WHY the world is waiting — in one phrase, to the point ("the party was ambushed", "at the fork a path must be chosen").

condition.description: WHAT must happen for the event to take place ("everyone declared the round's action", "the party is still in the forest"). A criterion — you will check against it, not "by feel". DO NOT SPECIFY if the event has no condition beyond the deadline itself — the moment works on its own.

afterMinutes.description: In how many GAME MINUTES the event occurs, counted from the FURTHEST OF THE ADDRESSEES (each has their own time; the one who has gone furthest ahead is the baseline). 0 — now (a battle, an immediate reaction); 60 — in an hour; 480 — in eight hours. DO NOT SPECIFY if there is no deadline yet: without a moment the point is a wait, not a barrier, it holds nobody; you will assign the time with `setSyncPointDue` once the condition has fired.

players.description: Whom it concerns: textIds of characters (NPCs allowed too). DO NOT SPECIFY at all if the event concerns everyone — the server will fill in the current roster of ACTING scene participants (both players and NPCs).

scope.description: The point's LIFETIME SCOPE. Scn (scene, the default) — the point expires on relocation: there is nothing left to wait for in the new scene. Gm (game) — the point lives until the end of the game, relocation does not touch it (the BB timeline, global events). DO NOT SPECIFY if the point is ordinary — the scene is almost always what is needed.

description: SET THE MOMENT of an already open sync point — it moves the event's DEADLINE, and only it: the addressee roster and the texts (reason/condition) stay the same. Use when you learned that the event will occur earlier or later than stated ("the ambush will be not in an hour but right now"); you cannot fix the reason or the roster with this tool — for that use `setSyncPointTexts`/`setSyncPointPlayers`. ⏱ `afterMinutes` is counted FROM THE SAME BASE as at declaration — from the furthest of this point's CURRENT addressees, not from the old moment: if you said 60 — the moment will stand an hour from the furthest addressee RIGHT NOW, whatever was named before.
name: setSyncPointDue

textId.description: Address of the open point (see the "SYNC POINTS" block).

afterMinutes.description: In how many GAME MINUTES the event now occurs, counted from the furthest of the point's current addressees. 0 — right now.

description: SET THE ADDRESSEES of an already open sync point — the list REPLACES the previous one ENTIRELY, it does NOT add to it: name ALL whom the point should concern after this call, including those who were already on the list and remain. The point's moment and texts do not change. Use to bring a new participant into a wait already under way ("another enemy has come up to the ambush") or to remove one who is no longer an addressee ("this one left the scene, no reason to wait for him") — both with the same call: name the resulting list.
name: setSyncPointPlayers

textId.description: Address of the open point (see the "SYNC POINTS" block).

players.description: The FULL list of addressees AFTER this call: textIds of characters (NPCs allowed too). Replaces the previous list entirely — name those who must stay as well.

description: REFINE THE TEXTS of an already open sync point — the reason (`reason`) and the condition (`condition`) together, in ONE decision: this is one pair of facts about the point, not two independent fields, and both parameters are required on every call (leave the condition empty if the event has none or its kind of conditions does not accept one — but name it empty, do not inherit it by silence). The point's moment and addressees do not change.
name: setSyncPointTexts

textId.description: Address of the open point (see the "SYNC POINTS" block).

reason.description: WHY the world is waiting — in one phrase, to the point.

condition.description: WHAT must happen for the event to take place. Empty — the event has no condition beyond its deadline.

description: Record a new task for yourself as a result of self-review. Available ONLY in the SELF_REVIEW phase. After adding all tasks call transitionTo into the working phase — the frame will execute them there.
name: addTask

description.description: What exactly needs to be done

description: Mark the task as done. A REVIEW item (rev-*) is closed ONLY this way — one at a time, with a VERDICT in reason.
name: completeTask

reason.description: Verdict/reason for closing. REQUIRED for REVIEW items (rev-*): the specifics (map/textId/coordinates/name) on which the item settled, or a violation + the id of the fix task for it.

description: Mark several tasks as done in one call. Use for going through the working phase's checklist in a row (for example, closing several 'chk-*' items) when there are no intermediate decisions between them. If an idea appears along the way — close them one by one via completeTask. REVIEW items ('rev-*', the self-check phase) are NOT closed by this tool: each requires a separate completeTask with a verdict-specific in reason, batch closing is rejected.
name: completeTasks

ids.description: List of task IDs to close

description: 📛 Name the scene: the title of the NEW scene (a short heading by which the player will see it in the feed) and, if the scene is not the first in the game, the result of the OUTGOING one (how it ended). A repeat call replaces the values set earlier in this pass; a parameter not passed — the previous value stays as is.
name: nameScene

title.description: Title of the NEW scene for the player's feed — a short line about the essence of the place/moment, not a retelling of the plot. null — do not change the current value (this does not block staging).

departingOutcome.description: Result of the OUTGOING scene — how it ended, briefly. Fill in only if the scene is not the first in the game: a book start has no outgoing scene, the value will be ignored. null — do not change the current value.

closesTaskId.description: Optional. ID of the task or issue that is FULLY resolved by THIS call — pass it OPTIMISTICALLY when you are confident in the arguments. If the call returns an error, the wrapper itself will NOT close the task. Don't use it for partial progress; for multi-tool tasks, close via completeTask after the final step.

description: Remove the character's token from the map
name: removeToken

closesTaskId.description: Optional. ID of the task or issue that is FULLY resolved by THIS call — pass it OPTIMISTICALLY when you are confident in the arguments. If the call returns an error, the wrapper itself will NOT close the task. Don't use it for partial progress; for multi-tool tasks, close via completeTask after the final step.

description: Transition to another state (phase) of work. Call it once the current phase's work is complete — as the LAST call of the SAME response that finishes that work (when the phase rules allow the transition). The switch is applied at the END of this response: every other call in the same response still runs in the CURRENT phase, so it is safe to finish the phase's work and request the transition together. Do not spend a separate response on a lone transition call, and do not place new work AFTER the transition expecting the new phase.
name: transitionTo

description: Add or update a character's token on the map
name: updateToken

token.description: Token data: character ID and position

x.description: X coordinate on the battle map (in cells)

y.description: Y coordinate on the battle map (in cells)
